sec: Treatment: maintenance, steroid equivalence and crisis regimen · p851

items.q: The drug of choice for maintenance in Addison's is:
items.exp: Oral hydrocortisone is DOC; others prednisolone, dexamethasone; fludrocortisone if MC deficiency present. (Book p851)

Fludrocortisone (when MC deficiency is present) is dosed at:
During fever or infection, the maintenance steroid dose should be:
items.exp: Fever or infection: double the dose. (Book p851)

items.q: On the day of surgery, the book advises:
items.exp: On day of surgery: 50 to 100 mg IV hydrocortisone; hospitalisation ↑ dose to 50–75 mg/day. (Book p851)

items.q: Match equivalent glucocorticoid doses — 1) Dexamethasone  2) Methylprednisolone  3) Prednisolone  4) Hydrocortisone … A) 20 mg  B) 0.75 mg  C) 4 mg  D) 5 mg
items.exp: 0.75 mg dexamethasone = 4 mg methylprednisolone = 5 mg prednisolone = 20 mg hydrocortisone = 25 mg cortisol. (Book p851)

items.q: In crisis, the FIRST-day hydrocortisone total (100 mg IV stat + 50 mg IV Q6H) equals:
items.exp: 100 mg immediately + 50 mg IV Q6H = 1st day 300 mg; then 200 mg (2nd), 100 mg (3rd), 50 mg (4th). (Book p851)

items.q: Match the crisis taper by day — 1) 2nd day  2) 3rd day  3) 4th day … A) 100 mg IV  B) 200 mg IV  C) 50 mg IV
items.exp: Day 2 = 200 mg IV, day 3 = 100 mg IV, day 4 = 50 mg IV, then oral 25 mg (10,10,5) for a week and 20 mg (10,5,5) maintenance ± fludrocortisone. (Book p851)

items.q: Crisis IV fluids are given as:
opts: 0.9% NS/DNS 1 L over 1 hour, then 2–3 L over the next 12 hours
items.exp: IV fluids: 0.9% NS/DNS 1 L over 1 hour, then 2–3 L over next 12 hours. (Book p851)

items.q: After a crisis is controlled, the oral step-down before maintenance is:
items.exp: Oral hydrocortisone 25 mg (10,10,5) for 1 week, then 20 mg (10,5,5) maintenance ± fludrocortisone. (Book p851)
